classification.difficultyReason: Identify vertices or perfect squares, sketch the quadratics, and distinguish all-real, empty and singleton solution sets using strict versus inclusive inequalities.

content.prompt:
[Trick questions]

Solve the following inequalities by sketching an appropriate graph.

answer.worked: The graph of $y=x^2+1$ opens upwards with minimum point $(0,1)$. It lies entirely above the $x$-axis, so the inequality holds for all real $x$.

spec.description: Solution graph entirely above the x-axis, with minimum labelled.

answer.worked: The graph of $y=x^2+4$ opens upwards with minimum point $(0,4)$. It never lies below the $x$-axis, so there are no solutions.

spec.description: Solution graph entirely above the x-axis, with minimum labelled.

answer.worked: The graph of $y=x^2$ touches the $x$-axis at $(0,0)$ and is otherwise above it. Hence $x^2\le0$ only when $x=0$.

spec.description: Solution graph touching the x-axis at its labelled minimum.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+2x+2&=(x+1)^2+1\end{align*}$$
The graph opens upwards with minimum point $(-1,1)$, so it lies entirely above the $x$-axis. The solution is all real $x$.

spec.description: Solution graph with positive minimum labelled below the curve.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}-x^2+2x-2&=-(x-1)^2-1\end{align*}$$
The graph opens downwards with maximum point $(1,-1)$. It lies entirely below the $x$-axis, so there are no solutions.

spec.description: Solution graph with negative maximum labelled above the curve.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}4x^2-4x+1&=(2x-1)^2\end{align*}$$
The upward-opening parabola touches the $x$-axis at $x=\frac12$ and is otherwise above it. Hence the only solution is $x=\frac12$.

spec.description: Solution graph touching the x-axis at the labelled double root.
